Dissatisfied with the reliefs granted under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, by the trial Court as well as by the appellate Court, the petitioner is now before this Court with this revision petition filed under Section 397 r/w Section 401 of Cr.P.C.
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On 07.03.2025, when this matter was taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner submitted that there is no instructions from the petitioner and hence the matter is adjourned to this day.
There was no representation for respondents 1 to 4 on 07.03.2025.

3. Today, when this matter is taken up for consideration, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner submitted that there is no instructions from the petitioner, even after sending a written intimation to her by the Counsel.
There is no representation for respondents 1 to 4.
Therefore, after hearing the learned Public Prosecutor, who is appearing for the 5 th respondent, this revision petition is taken up for orders.
4. I have carefully perused the impugned order and the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate Court respectively 2025:KER:72722 and also the materials on record.
The marriage of the petitioner with the 1st respondent was held on 28.08.2005 as per the customs and ceremonies prevailing in their community.

According to the petitioner, a child was born in their wedlock, who was aged two Sunainaz vs Faizal Ahammed on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49807001/
2 years at the time of filing the petition before the trial Court.

In the petition filed under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, the revision petitioner claimed that her parents had gifted 150 sovereigns of gold ornaments, and a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- to the 1st respondent at the time of marriage.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
She alleged ill treatment from the hands of respondents 1 to 4,
claiming more dowry from her parental house.
Even a criminal case under Sections 498A, 324, 323 r/w Section 34 of IPC was registered against the 1st respondent and his family members, at the instance of the petitioner.
5. Before the trial Court, PWs 1 to 3 were examined, and Exts.P1 to P8 were marked from the side of the petitioner.
From the side of the 1st respondent, RW1 was examined and Exts.D1 and D2 documents were marked.
The petitioner is authorized to received the said amount on behalf of the minor child.
(iii) The prayer for return of gold and Rs.2,00,000/- is hereby rejected.
(iv) Prayer for compensation is also hereby rejected.
(v) The petition against respondents 2 to 4 is hereby dismissed.

(vi) Prayer for protection order is hereby rejected."
6. Dissatisfied with the order of the trial Court, the petitioner approached the appellate Court, and by the impugned judgment dated 06.08.2014, the appellate Court modified the order of the trial Court as under;

"1. The appellant is granted an order to recover a sum of Rs.30,000/- with 6% per annum interest thereon from the date of MC till realisation from respondent No.1 as compensation for mental agony consequent to physical and mental assault suffered during the course of cohabitation.
2. In other receipts, the appeal fails, and the order of the trial court is upheld.

3. The appellant is at liberty to prosecute her claim relating 2025:KER:72722 to 150 sovereigns of gold ornaments allegedly worn by her and allegedly misappropriated by the first respondent in the proceedings she has instituted under section 3 of Muslim Sunainaz vs Faizal Ahammed on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49807001/
3 Women (Protection on Divorce) Act."
7.
From the impugned judgment and the materials on record, it is evident that the petitioner remarried on 09.09.2012 and she has been residing with her 2nd husband, since then.
Noting all these aspects, the trial Court as well as the appellate Court granted the reliefs in favour of the petitioner.

Moreover, the appellate Court granted liberty to the petitioner to prosecute her claim relating to 150 sovereigns of gold ornaments allegedly worn by her and allegedly misappropriated by the 1 st respondent in the proceedings she has instituted under section 3 of the Muslim Women (Protection on Divorce) Act.
On re-appreciation of the materials on record, I find no reason to hold that there is any illegality or impropriety in the finding arrived at by the appellate Court.

Therefore,
the revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
In the result, this revision petition stands dismissed.
